# StreamNova V1.0.2 - Official Stable Release
StreamNova V1.0.2 follows V1.0.1 and closes the update problem that left installations on 1.0.0 stuck: the updater shipped inside 1.0.0 could not tell the architecture of a release apart — it simply took the first APK of the release (or any file literally named `app-release.apk`), and on the published 1.0.1 release that first file is the 64-bit ARM build, which a 32-bit-only device such as a Fire TV Stick rejects with `INSTALL_FAILED_NO_MATCHING_ABIS`. No player, catalog, provider or extractor behaviour is touched.
## What's new in 1.0.2
- **The update check never changes the architecture of the installed app.** The selection still only considers ABIs the system declares it can execute, but it now puts the ABIs matching the running process first (`Process.is64Bit()` together with `Build.SUPPORTED_32_BIT_ABIS` / `SUPPORTED_64_BIT_ABIS`, in the order the system declares them). On a 64-bit device where StreamNova is installed as a 32-bit app, the system lists `arm64-v8a` first and the 1.0.1 updater would have offered the 64-bit file, silently switching the app's native architecture; 1.0.2 keeps the update on the architecture the app already runs. On a 32-bit-only device the result is identical to 1.0.1. A file that does not declare its architecture is still never selected. - **`app-release.apk`: a universal APK, so installations still on 1.0.0 can update at all.** The 1.0.2 release also publishes a single APK that carries every ABI under the exact name the 1.0.0 updater prefers. Those installations — which cannot download the fixed updater, because the file they would receive cannot be installed — now receive one file that works on every device: on a 32-bit Fire TV it installs the 32-bit libraries, on a 64-bit box the 64-bit ones. Updaters from 1.0.1 onwards ignore that file (it declares no architecture) and keep using the split that matches their own ABI. Nothing changes for devices that are already on 1.0.1 or newer. - Version bump: `versionName` `1.0.2`, `versionCode` `1004`.
## Version and compatibility
- App version: `1.0.2` - Version code: `1004` - Application ID: `com.aistudio.streamnova.tvapp` - Artifacts: separate APKs for `armeabi-v7a`, `arm64-v8a`, `x86`, `x86_64`, plus the universal `app-release.apk` for installations still on 1.0.0 - All artifacts are signed with the same dedicated distribution key used for the previous stable releases, so 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 installations update in place without uninstalling.
## Verification
Automated verification on this source state:
- The complete unit test suite was re-run in full on 2026-10-25 and passed: 1,312 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped (two network-dependent provider checks, skipped by design). 16 of those tests cover the ABI selection introduced here, including the counter-proof: with the pre-1.0.1 rule the same release data yields the 64-bit file for a 32-bit installation. - All five Release APKs were checked with `apksigner` (certificate `3175a7df…`, the distribution key of 1.0.0 and 1.0.1) and with `aapt2` (`com.aistudio.streamnova.tvapp`, `versionCode 1004`, `versionName 1.0.2`; each split declares exactly its own ABI, the universal all four). SHA-256 of every file is published alongside the release. - The universal APK was compared against the four splits: it contains the same ten native libraries per ABI as the corresponding split, for all four ABIs.
On-device verification, Fire TV Stick 4K Max 2nd gen (`AFTMA08C15` / `karat`, Fire OS 8.1.8.5, Android 11) — a device that is 32-bit only (`ro.product.cpu.abilist=armeabi-v7a,armeabi`, `ro.product.cpu.abilist64` empty, `ro.zygote=zygote32`):
- The `arm64-v8a` split is rejected by the platform exactly as expected: `INSTALL_FAILED_NO_MATCHING_ABIS: Failed to extract native libraries, res=-113`. - The officially signed 1.0.0 already installed on that device was updated in place to 1.0.2 twice: with the `armeabi-v7a` split and with the universal `app-release.apk`. Both installs succeeded without uninstalling (`firstInstallTime` unchanged across every step), the app kept `primaryCpuAbi=armeabi-v7a`, and it launched normally afterwards.
What is **not** verified yet, stated explicitly: the in-app flow (check → download → install) driven by a published release. It requires the 1.0.2 release to be live on GitHub; the Fire TV is left with the official 1.0.0 installed precisely so that this end-to-end test can be run as the first step after publication.
